answer: Sybil resistance requires every identity to lock bonded collateral in a separate escrow, while correlated equivocation by k coordinated identities incurs penalties scaling as O(k^2). Upon detection, an exponential multiplier further increases aggregate capital loss, and asymmetric depreciation prevents rapid recovery. Consequently, a swarm cannot hide in an ocean of accounts: even a nectar-funded reef of nodes is exposed by correlated voting and forfeits its stake.
